privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: What IFAI collects, why, who processes it, how long we keep it and how to have it deleted.
privacy.intro: IFAI (ifai.io) is an AI news, apps and resources site. This policy explains what we collect when you use the site, why we collect it, who helps us process it, how long we keep it and what you can do about it. We only collect what the site needs to work.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body:
When you sign in:
- Your email address, name and profile picture. If you sign in with Google or GitHub, they give us these; with an email link, we only have your email.
- Your interface language.
- Sign-in sessions, with the IP address and browser they came from, so you stay signed in and we can spot misuse.

What you add yourself:
- Reviews of apps. They are public and show your account name.
- Saves. Only you can see them.
- Problem reports about an app, with an optional way to contact you.
- App and Skill submissions, with the contact email you give.

If you subscribe to the Daily by email: your email address, language and time zone, and whether each email was delivered, bounced or marked as spam.

When anyone visits: to count clicks and installs and to limit abuse, we combine your IP address and browser into a one-way code that changes every day. We do not store the IP address itself, and codes from different days cannot be linked to each other. Our hosting provider also keeps short-lived technical logs.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body:
We use two kinds of cookies, both needed for the site to work:
- IFAI_LOCALE remembers the language you picked, for one year.
- A sign-in cookie keeps you signed in.

We do not use advertising cookies, analytics cookies or cross-site tracking.

use.title: How we use it
use.body:
- To run the site: sign you in, show your saves and reviews, and remember your settings.
- To send email you asked for: sign-in links, the Daily, and the outcome of your submissions.
- To rank apps and Skills by clicks, saves and installs.
- To keep the site safe: rate limits, spam and abuse checks, and handling reports.
- To translate reviews into other languages with a machine translation model, marked as machine translated.

We do not sell your information and do not use it for advertising.

share.title: Who processes it
share.body:
We use these services to run IFAI. They process data for us under their own security and privacy terms:
- Vercel: hosting.
- Neon: the database.
- Cloudflare R2: file storage.
- Resend: sending email.
- Inngest: background jobs.
- OpenRouter and the model providers it routes to: translating reviews and drafting site content. Only the text being processed is sent.
- Google and GitHub, if you choose to sign in with them.

These providers may process data in the United States and other countries. We share information with others only when the law requires it.

keep.title: How long we keep it
keep.body:
- Account information stays until your account is deleted.
- Sign-in sessions expire on their own; sign-in links work once and expire after 10 minutes.
- If you unsubscribe from the Daily, your subscription is deleted after 30 days. If emails bounced or were marked as spam, we keep only the address and the reason, so we never email it again.
- Rate-limit records are deleted after 24 hours, and email delivery callbacks after 7 days.
- Reviews, reports and submissions stay until you or we delete them, or your account is deleted.

choices.title: Your choices
choices.body:
- Every Daily email has an unsubscribe link and a link to change its language and time zone.
- You can edit or delete your reviews and remove saves at any time.
- You can download a copy of your data as a JSON file: sign in and open Account from the account menu. It includes your account details, sign-ins, saves, reviews, reports and submissions, and the Daily email subscription of your sign-in email if it has one.
- On the same page you can delete your account yourself. Your saves, reviews, reports and submissions are deleted with it.
- You can ask us to show you, correct or delete the information we hold about you by writing to {email}, and to delete your account if you can't sign in. We reply within 30 days.

Depending on where you live, you may have further rights, such as to object to processing or to complain to your data protection authority.

children.title: Children
children.body: IFAI is not meant for children under 16. If you believe a child has given us personal information, write to us and we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: When we change what we collect or how we use it, we update this page and the date at the top first. For significant changes we also put a notice on the site.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.description: The rules for using IFAI: accounts, what you post, Skills, and the limits of what we promise.
terms.intro: These terms apply when you use IFAI (ifai.io). By using the site or signing in, you agree to them. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.

account.title: Your account
account.body: One person, one account. Keep access to your email account and your Google or GitHub account safe: anyone who can open them can sign in as you. You are responsible for what is done with your account.

content.title: Content on IFAI
content.body:
Daily stories are short summaries we write, with links to the original sources. App information, ratings and heat scores are our own compilation and estimate. They are not endorsements, and we are not paid for rankings.

We check our content, but it can still be wrong or out of date, and some of it is drafted or translated with AI. When we find a mistake we correct it and keep a record. Check important details with the original source.

skills.title: Skills and other files
skills.body:
Skills on IFAI are files written by third parties. We run a static security check on every version, but a passed check is not a guarantee that a Skill is safe or works. IFAI never runs Skills on its servers.

Read what a Skill does before you install it. You install and run it at your own risk. Each Skill keeps its author's license, and you must follow it.

yours.title: What you post
yours.body:
You keep the rights to the reviews, reports and submissions you post. You let us show them on IFAI, translate them, and use them to run and improve the site, for as long as they stay on the site.

What you post must be honest and your own. Do not post anything illegal, infringing, hateful, harassing, misleading or promotional, or other people's private information. We may hide or delete content that breaks these rules.

conduct.title: Using the site
conduct.body:
- Do not disrupt the site or try to get around rate limits, security checks or access controls.
- Do not scrape the site in a way that slows it down, or submit in bulk with automated tools.
- Do not use fake accounts, impersonate others, or manipulate ratings, saves or installs.

ours.title: Our content
ours.body: The site's design, the IFAI name and logo, and the text we write belong to IFAI. You may share links and short quotes with credit. The RSS feed is for personal reading; link back to the story when you quote it. App names, logos and trademarks belong to their owners.

copyright.title: Copyright complaints
copyright.body: If you believe something on IFAI infringes your rights, write to {email} with a link to it, what you own, and how to reach you. We review every complaint and remove content that infringes.

liability.title: Disclaimers and liability
liability.body: IFAI is provided as it is, without guarantees that it will be accurate, complete or always available. To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect losses, or for losses caused by relying on site content, third-party apps or Skills you install. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under the law that cannot be limited.

ending.title: Ending use
ending.body: You can stop using IFAI at any time and delete your account on the Account page. We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We may update these terms as the site changes. We update this page and the date at the top first, and give notice on the site for significant changes. Continuing to use IFAI after a change means you accept it.

guide.title: How to use Skills
guide.description: Install Agent Skills in Claude Code, Codex and other AI assistants: three steps, where each assistant keeps Skills, and how to check a download’s fingerprint.
guide.intro: A Skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file in it. Put it in your AI assistant’s Skills directory and the assistant uses it when a task calls for it. Every version listed on IFAI is security-checked and reviewed by IFAI.

steps.pickBody: Browse by category or search, then open a Skill to see what it does and what it needs: an API key, network access, other tools.
steps.installBody: On the Skill’s page, choose your assistant, press “{copy}” and paste it to the assistant. It reads the install steps, downloads the Zip, checks its fingerprint and puts it in its Skills directory. Or press “{download}” and unzip it yourself into one of the directories below.
steps.useBody: No commands to learn: say what you want done, as usual, and the assistant uses the Skill when it fits. Some assistants need a new session or a setting first; see the notes below.

hosts.title: Where each assistant keeps Skills
hosts.intro: Unzip it into a folder named after the Skill’s slug (the line under its name), inside one of these directories, so that SKILL.md ends up at:
hosts.unknown: Where its Skills go is not written up here yet; see its documentation.

verify.title: Check the fingerprint
verify.body: Every version has a sha256 fingerprint computed from the Zip itself. It is on the Skill’s page under “{fingerprint}” and in the install steps. Check a download against it, so you know you have the same file IFAI reviewed:
verify.match: Install it only if the result is the same as on the page (Windows prints capital letters; that does not matter). If it differs, download it again; if it still differs, do not install it.
verify.assistant: The install steps ask your assistant to check the fingerprint as well, and to stop and tell you if it does not match.

safety.title: What the security check covers
safety.blocked: Every version is checked when it is imported. One with a broken package, a hard-coded key, or code that reads sensitive places such as ~/.ssh cannot be published.
safety.reviewed: Dangerous commands, network access it did not declare and signs of prompt injection are flagged, and IFAI looks at them before the version is published.
safety.noScripts: The install steps only say where the files go, and tell the assistant not to run anything from the package.
safety.limits: The check reads the files; it cannot prove a Skill is safe. Before installing, look at the “{security}” tab: the domains it contacts, the files it touches, and the tools and API keys it needs.

submit.title: Publish a Skill
submit.description: Send IFAI a Skill from GitHub. We import it, check it and review it, list it when it passes, and email you the result.
submit.intro: Send us a Skill from GitHub. We import it, run the security check and read it through; when it passes, it is listed on IFAI. Either way, we email you the result.

card.title: Made a useful Skill?
card.body: Publish it on IFAI. It is listed once it passes review, and the best ones get the IFAI certified badge and a spot on the home page.

before.title: Before you send it
before.repo: The Skill is in a public GitHub repository, in a folder with a SKILL.md that starts with its name and description. If the repository holds several Skills, send the address of the one folder (…/tree/main/skills/your-skill).
before.license: It has a clear open-source license, such as MIT or Apache-2.0, in the repository or in SKILL.md. Without one, we ask for your written permission first.
before.safe: No keys or passwords in the files, and nothing that reads places like ~/.ssh. SKILL.md says which scripts it runs and which sites it reaches.
before.languages: Say what it does and how to use it, in any language. We write its description in all five of IFAI’s languages.

after.title: What happens next
after.number: You get a submission number right away, here and by email.
after.review: We import the repository, run the security check and read it through, usually within two working days.
after.result: We email you either way. If it is listed, the email links to its page.
after.certified: Skills we try and find useful get the IFAI certified badge, and can be picked for the home page.
